origin: Reviewed BAR project seed from durable chapters, approved horizon, and bounded 2026-10-01 reports; summaries are retained here so temporary reports are not the sole truth anchor.

items.title: BAR command and observation ownership
items.statement: BAR content and synced Lua own game policy; Recoil owns simulation and the native AI ABI; HighBar owns the CircuitAI gateway and engine-thread dispatch; FSBar owns broker/browser authority and WASM execution. Admission, delivery, native acceptance, dispatch, and observed effect are separate signals.

scope.applicability: navigation architecture, not authorization or runtime success

evidence.summary: Durable overview records the cross-project route and separate evidence boundaries.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Stock baseline selected for useful play
items.statement: Root recorded the stock Recoil route as the local useful-play direction. This is a project decision, not evidence that the stock engine or overlay is merged, installed, selected, loaded, or natively accepted.

scope.applicability: current local project direction only

evidence.summary: Approved horizon records the later stock selection and requires older undecided history not to override it.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Stock queue evidence omits timeout
items.statement: The stock evidence scheme contains domain, command id, options.coded, tag, and ordered finite float32 parameter bits. Timeout is unavailable and must never be fabricated as zero or imported through a full-native-tuple fallback.

scope.applicability: stock scheme 2 supported-field boundary

evidence.summary: Corrected contract review states timeout unavailable, exact scheme 2, and no fallback.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.statement: The durable lineage separates upstream stock 2639eedac7d1fd67d793ec93ebd27f014f336a14, rally extension 7555c836e0457b04100b20149497d088dd9c2ca7, and custom observer candidate 2572991c77110f8d9893253051aa8d8958b7aec6. items.title: Retained engine artifacts do not establish loaded runtime
items.statement: A registered source, retained executable hash, or configured pin does not establish which engine binary a current process loaded. Exact selected and observed process artifact identity is required before naming the runtime variant.

scope.applicability: all native and crash claims

evidence.summary: Lineage update explicitly separates source, retained artifact, configured selection, and observed loaded runtime.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.statement: The custom atomic replacement and observer guarantees remain historical optional work. The current stock direction does not activate FR1-FR6 or transfer their all-or-none, refund, fence, replay, or peer-service guarantees.

evidence.summary: Corrected contract review keeps optional FR1-FR6 open and inactive.

items.title: Clean HighBar build lacked generated protobuf sources
items.statement: A clean HighBar checkout had no ignored generated protobuf files, leaving highbar_proto with an empty source list. The bounded repair pinned eight inputs and exact protoc/gRPC generators, generated and verified 32 outputs, and retained HIGHBAR_REQUIRE_WIRE_DEPS; it did not compile or install an engine.

scope.applicability: named clean build repair only

evidence.summary: Test report records the clean-checkout cause, pins, refusals, and passed configure gate.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Build7 custody was broken by an in-place objcopy mistake
items.statement: A read-intended objcopy invocation omitted a distinct output operand and rewrote both build6 and build7 spring-dedicated files in place. Immediate SHA checks detected the incident; contaminated binaries were inadmissible and historical manifests were retained.

scope.applicability: specific 2026-10-01 custody incident

evidence.summary: Incident report records the exact command mistake, changed hashes, and stop condition.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Build7 dedicated identity correction
items.statement: The original claim that build7 dedicated reproduced build6 was false. The correction records distinct dedicated and headless hashes, an inherited predecessor plugin, and the need to rebuild and read back the successor plugin before any repin.

scope.applicability: corrected build7 artifact set

evidence.summary: Correction preserves the false sentence as history and supplies the exact comparison table.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Build7 dedicated custody recovery reproduced protected hashes
items.statement: The recovery report records isolated relinking from existing objects, exact reproduction of the protected build6 and build7 dedicated hashes, and restoration only after equality. This is reported artifact recovery, not native gameplay acceptance.

scope.applicability: named custody recovery; no native effect

evidence.summary: Recovery addendum records protected copies, isolated linker replay, exact matches, and bounded restoration.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Runtime bootstrap must derive binding from owned producers
items.statement: Static preparation can freeze paths, hashes, plans, ports, and deadlines, but live PID/start identity, session credentials, factory setup, producer capture, and full native binding must come from authenticated owned runtime producers. Copying supplied JSON into expected binding defeats independent admission.

scope.applicability: future native bootstrap design

evidence.summary: Feasibility review traces the missing runtime binding derivation and closed authenticated route.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Selected interval cannot be fabricated from an all-count plan
items.statement: The preserved Count1/2/4 plan is not equivalent to one selected native run. A one-count supervisor cannot satisfy unselected rows with invented sessions, credentials, lifetimes, or future observations; selected-interval materialization needs an explicit authenticated contract.

scope.applicability: negative feasibility finding for Count1/2/4 bootstrap

evidence.summary: Review identifies all-count validation versus one-count runtime mismatch and rejects placeholder handoff reuse.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Initial stock Lua observer candidate is source-blocked
items.statement: Candidate 2a7ae7f passed 11 mock-Spring tests under system Lua 5.5 and packaged deterministic overlay bytes, but independent stock review found three blockers: removed rawget in synced Lua, float-number loss in SHA/float encoding, and refusal of legal actor ID 0. The package is not stock-runtime compatible or natively accepted.

scope.applicability: blocked initial candidate and generic-Lua tests only

evidence.summary: Independent review records 11/11 generic tests plus three exact stock compatibility defects.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Fixture ABI success does not establish deployed engine ABI
items.statement: Tests using the host system Lua 5.5 cannot establish behavior under stock Recoil synced Lua, where globals are restricted and LUA_NUMBER is float. Boundary tests must match the deployed engine ABI and numeric model.

scope.applicability: all Lua bridge qualification

evidence.summary: Review contrasts system Lua 5.5 fixtures with stock restricted float-number Lua and gives counterexamples.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Stock CallRules reaches the synced LuaRules handle
items.statement: The stock AI callback supplies aiTeam and LuaRules CallRules forwards to syncedLuaHandle. A generic comment calling the AI call-in unsynced does not override that explicit dispatch, so moving the reader to unsynced code would be the wrong repair.

scope.applicability: stock source route as documented by independent source review

evidence.summary: Review records exact callback, LuaRules handle, and gadget dispatch source locations.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Stock float32 encoding should use byte-preserving engine support
items.statement: Stock VFS.PackF32 copies float bytes into a Lua string and can support an exact byte codec. Full uint32 assembly in stock float-number Lua loses low bits; SHA-256 needs bounded exact limbs or another exact compatible implementation rather than a different hash algorithm.

scope.applicability: repair direction, still requiring source review and native qualification

evidence.summary: Review identifies VFS.PackF32 and bounded limb SHA as compatible repair directions.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: What still blocks stock native acceptance?
items.statement: Open gates include a stock-compatible Lua repair, exact overlay discovery and loaded content identity, native parser and plugin compatibility, catalogue/content/profile/actor-lifetime binding, post-acquisition reread and queue equality, exact selected engine identity, and all required local/generated/imported-module native journeys.

scope.applicability: open questions after source-contract acceptance

evidence.summary: Contract review lists parser, limits, identity, reread, compatibility, and native gates.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

evidence.summary: Lua review adds source-compatible codec, actor0, discovery, parser join, and native gates.
evidence.scope: Only the named document and stated attempt; no broader runtime inference.

items.title: Stock native reader source candidate compiles against exact Recoil
items.statement: HighBar candidate 0e0e84fb1d8362b49630afd5a958ba49411b3aac (tree 7350a0b03fea94fd66efd266c64140a9c49978b7) compiled and linked its strict stock queue reader against unpatched Recoil 2639eedac7d1fd67d793ec93ebd27f014f336a14; focused reader and tactical native state tests passed.
